Rindeil's mansion

Setting

Rindeil’s mansion provides temporary shelter among an eccentric collector’s spiders. Karim offers gossip and useful contacts. The safety is conditional: when imperial searches threaten the estate, Rindeil withdraws his welcome. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Shelter at Rindeil’s estate

Rindeil welcomes Kel and her companion to his estate. Kir’s learning gives them common ground, though the collector’s chief concern remains his spiders. Karim, who manages the household and formerly performed on stage, becomes a source of contacts and rumours about another Joon. Feiruz helps Kir hide his conspicuous face beneath cloth, exploiting the fear of disease. Rindeil’s requests include obtaining a meteorite sample in exchange for a rare specimen for his collection. This period of refuge lets Kir search for information, but its safety depends on the owner’s willingness to risk his household. [2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8]

Zara’s affairs

The merchant Zara is another of Kel’s Suslanger contacts. Her side of the story involves a blackmailer, a threatened caravan and contraband that must be recovered before the authorities inspect it. The conversations distinguish successful recovery from arriving too late; the account of the caravan therefore depends on the outcome of that errand. Later, Zara’s interest in a scholar draws Kir into a scheme against Kehel. These dealings develop alongside the search for a Joon, rather than forming a single inevitable sequence of victories. [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16]

Feiruz’s last rescue

Feiruz asks Kir to repay his help by rescuing his imprisoned fiancée Aliya. He dies during the escape. Kel urges the grieving Aliya to avenge him and identifies the man who struck the fatal blow. Kir objects to deliberate revenge, but their companions insist on their code. The death of the prison commandant brings searches across the city. Fearing for his collection, Rindeil withdraws his protection, though he says Kir may return once the danger passes. Aliya then leads Kir and Kel to the Last Shelter and speaks for them before Brother Khatul. [17, 18, 19, 4, 20]

The report and the passage to Gipath

Karim’s rumour about the missing red-skinned youth becomes a document recovered from the necromancers. It records transformation and teleportation before the attack on the scholars’ mansion, with Gipath as the destination. Kir decides to follow that Joon. Sahilia supplies enlistment papers, and Kel refuses to be left behind, passing as a young man herself. Sergeant Zairak puts them through military training in Death Canyon. Their performance earns a courier assignment to the Gipath expedition. Sealed orders and a portal pass finally let them leave Suslanger under the authority of the same empire that enslaved them. [8, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27]
